  2. A customer to sell to exists; if none does, create one first: top menu Customers -> New Customer, enter a Name (e.g. "4 Star Truck Repair") and click Save.
  3. A part sale created on or after the release, carrying a part with a core charge. Seed it with these standard steps:
  4. ↳ Open Part Sales from the main menu and start a New Part Sale; select the customer (e.g. "4 Star Truck Repair").
  5. ↳ On the Parts tab, click Add Part; set the Description (e.g. "Water Pump") and the Sell Price to a test amount (e.g. $517.55).
  6. ↳ In the Core column of that row, enter a Core Charge greater than 0 (e.g. $79.99), then save the row.
  7. ↳ Order the part, then Receive it (special-order) or Pick it (inventory), so Return Core becomes available.
154587.custom_steps:
1. On the part sale Parts grid, find the core row and its Actions cell.
  2. Click Return Core in the Actions cell.
  3. Read the core row's Status badge afterwards.
  4. Open the Finance tab, set the toggle to Estimate/Invoice, and read the part row, the Core charge child and the Core credit child, plus the Summary.
  5. Open Parts -> Returns and check for a new return.
154587.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • The core row shows a single action, Return Core, in the same Actions cell every other primary action uses; clicking it credits the core.
  • The core charge stays on the document and a second child row, "Core credit", is added crediting the same amount; the grid's core row now shows the Returned badge, and a return appears in Parts -> Returns.
  • On the document the credit prints indented behind ↳ as a negative amount (e.g. "↳ Core credit 1 -$79.99 -$79.99") directly beneath the "↳ Core charge" row; with the example data the Summary reads Parts $517.55, GST (5%) $25.88, Total $543.43.
